title: Playing solo in clubs in the sixties and his ambitions
summary: As rock and roll changed the business, Thompson played solo piano wherever he could find bookings and hopes for an appreciative audience.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And then of course when you came back through the sixties, I mean after that you played clubs all over, didn't you?

I played wherever I could find an engagement. The music business started to changing at that point, they were coming into this new found of rock and roll popularity and so forth. And so I just more or less strummed around as a solo player, you might say, [and] different clubs wherever I could find a booking. And the fact of the matter is I went back to my original playing solo piano, which I really enjoy because during these periods I get a chance to express myself more.

Well, you have so much -- you know, you have a great deal to offer, I mean, with all of that experience back of you there is that much more really that you can accomplish, I guess, after that much behind you, comparatively speaking. Wouldn't you say that's true?
Well, I don't know how to appraise

my own playing, except that I started to play music because I enjoyed it, and I haven't lost my love for playing music. I love to play music, the kind of music that I know, and I understand and can play well. And I would like to continue on playing the kind of music I love, and I would like to feel that I would find an appreciative audience wherever I am, will enjoy my efforts. And that is the height of my ambition at this time.
